transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... I'm just really worn down. It’s been a year of this. I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is... changing things. With my dad’s lab results. Or holding parts of them back. My family, the doctors... they all keep telling me the numbers are fine. But I know what I saw. The chart doesn’t match. And trying to get anyone to see that is just... it's wearing me down.

When your family and the doctors tell you the lab numbers are fine, do you think there's any possibility they could be right and you might be mistaken about what you saw? Or are you completely certain that something is being changed or hidden?

I'm not mistaken. 

I... I know what I saw. Like I said, it doesn't matter how many of them tell me the numbers are fine. The chart just doesn't match. I wouldn't have spent the last year trying to prove someone is changing his results if I wasn't sure.
Have you ever considered that maybe your mind could be playing tricks on you, or that stress over your dad's health might be making you see patterns that aren't really there?

No. I haven't. 

I... look, I draw blood for a living. I know how labs work. Stress doesn't change the actual files. Someone in the system is holding back his real numbers. The chart doesn't match what it should. 

My mind isn't playing tricks. I'm just... I'm just tired of everyone trying to tell me it's not happening.
Besides what you've noticed with your dad's lab charts, have you been hearing voices, seeing things, or experiencing any other unusual perceptions that others around you don't seem to notice?

No. I don't... I don't hear voices. Or see things. 

Nothing like that. I'm just talking about what's in the files.

When you think about someone changing your dad's lab results, do you have a clear picture in your mind of HOW they're doing it—like, what specific steps or methods would they have to use to change those files?

I don't know exactly how they do it. I just know that they are. 

I mean... they have access. It's a computer system. If someone wants to change a number, they just... log in and change it. I don't know the exact steps. I just know what the results should be, and what they actually say.

Besides what's happening with your dad's lab results, do you believe there are other things going on—like other people being involved in this, or other situations where things are being hidden or manipulated in ways connected to this?

No. It's... it's just my dad's labs. 

I haven't noticed anything else. I don't really pay attention to... other things. I'm just focused on his charts.
Do you have any ideas about who specifically in the clinic system might be doing this, or why they would want to change your dad's lab results?

I don't know who. I... I couldn't give you a name. 

And I don't know why they would. It doesn't make any sense to me either. I just... I don't know. I only know that the numbers aren't what they're supposed to be. That's all I can tell you.

How much of your day or week do you spend thinking about your dad's lab results or trying to investigate what's happening with them? Has this taken over most of your time, or is it something you think about but can still do other things?

I... I mean, I still go to work. I haven't missed any of my phlebotomy shifts. 

I still pay my bills and do what I need to do. I take care of myself. It's just... when I have free time, I look at the charts. But it hasn't stopped me from doing my normal day-to-day things. I just... I do what I have to do.

When you think about the lab results not matching, have you worked out a detailed explanation for how this all fits together—like, does it connect to other things, or have you figured out a logical chain of events that explains why this is happening?

I haven't... I haven't worked anything out. Like I said, I don't know why or how. 

It's just the numbers. I don't have some big theory. I just know what I see on the screen.

When you think about someone in the clinic changing your dad's lab results, have you thought about what someone would gain or benefit from doing that? Or do you have any sense of who might want to do this and why they'd want to?

I... I think I just said that. I don't know who it is. And I don't know what they'd get out of it. 

I haven't thought about it like that. I just know the numbers are wrong. That's all.

When you think about your dad's lab results being changed, do you have a clear picture of the whole situation—like, does it all make sense together as one connected story? Or does it feel more like separate pieces that don't quite fit together?

I don't really... look at it like a story. It's not a story. 

It's just pieces, I guess. The numbers on the screen. I don't know how it all fits together. I just know what I'm looking at.

When you think about the lab results being changed, do you feel like you understand how it all connects together—like, does one piece lead to another piece, and it all makes sense as one complete picture? Or is it more like you just notice the numbers are wrong without understanding how the whole thing fits together?

I feel like... you keep asking me the exact same thing. 

I don't have a picture. I just... I draw blood for a living, I know what labs are supposed to look like. I just see that his are wrong. I don't know how it all connects. I don't know how else to explain it to you.

When you look at your dad's lab results and think about them being changed, do you feel completely certain about this one specific thing—that the numbers are wrong—or do you also have beliefs connected to this, like ideas about why someone would target your dad specifically, or what the purpose of changing his labs might be?

I... we just went over this. I don't know why anyone would target him. 

I don't have any ideas about a purpose or... whatever else you're looking for. I am just certain the numbers are wrong. That's all I have to say about it.

When you're at work or in other places, do you ever get the sense that people are watching you, talking about you, or treating you differently because of what's happening with your dad's lab results? Or does this situation stay completely separate from how you experience other parts of your life?

I don't... no one is watching me. It's not like that. 

But things are different, I guess. My family has started leaving me out of planning his appointments lately. And at work... I feel like I'm not being considered for lab supervision anymore. They think I make record issues too confrontational. 

That's really all I've noticed.

When your family started leaving you out of your dad's appointment planning, and when you weren't considered for lab supervision at work, do you think those things happened because people found out about your concerns with the lab results and are trying to stop you? Or do you see those as separate things that happened for other reasons?

I don't know... I guess they're just separate things. 

My family probably just... they don't want to deal with me asking questions about the labs. And work is just work. I don't think anyone is trying to stop me. I just... I don't know why you're trying to make it into this big conspiracy. I just know the numbers are wrong.

When your family started leaving you out of your dad's appointments and you weren't considered for lab supervision, do you think those things happened on purpose—like people are deliberately trying to keep you away because of what you know about the lab results?

I thought I just answered that. No. 

Nobody is deliberately doing anything to keep me away. They just... don't want to deal with it. I don't know why we keep going over this. That's all it is.

Do you think someone might be changing your dad's lab results because they want to harm him, or because they have something against him personally? Or do you think it's just something happening with the system itself, without any connection to your dad specifically?

I don't... I don't know why you keep asking me things like this. 

No one is trying to hurt him. He's just... he's just an old man. Why would anyone care about him personally? It's just... the numbers. The numbers in the system don't match what they should be. That's all. I don't know who is doing it or why. I just know it's happening.

Besides the lab results, do you believe there are other ways people might be acting against you or deceiving you in your life—like at work, with your family, or anywhere else? Or is it really just about your dad's lab numbers?

No... it's just the labs. I don't know why you keep digging for other things. 

For the past year, I've just... I've only been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing them. Or holding parts of his results back. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine—the doctors, my family—but they aren't. I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. 

It's just... it's really wearing me down. That's all this is about. Just the numbers.
If you went back and looked at your dad's lab results again right now, is there any chance at all that you might have misread them the first time, or is that completely impossible?

I didn't misread them. 

I know what I saw. I draw blood for a living, I look at these kinds of numbers all day. I... I know they don't match. I've spent a year trying to get someone to just listen and see that the clinic system is altering them or hiding things. But everyone just keeps telling me they're fine. It's... it's exhausting. But I didn't misread them. That's impossible.

doctor.question: When your family started leaving you out of your dad's appointments and you weren't considered for lab supervision, do you think those things happened on purpose—like people are deliberately trying to keep you away because of what you know about the lab results?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient believes the family and coworkers' actions are deliberate attempts to keep her away because of what she knows (persecutory/conspiratorial beliefs). The patient's profile covers functional impairment (family leaving her out, work not considering her for supervision) but does not specifically detail whether she believes these actions are a deliberate, targeted conspiracy against her due to her knowledge, beyond what she has already stated (that they just think she's too confrontational/asking too many questions).

patient.answer:
I thought I just answered that. No. 

Nobody is deliberately doing anything to keep me away. They just... don't want to deal with it. I don't know why we keep going over this. That's all it is.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has any ideas about persecution or harm directed at their father specifically (which would suggest F22.0 with persecutory content) versus having a purely circumscribed false belief about lab manipulation without broader persecutory ideation (which would suggest F22.9).
doctor.question: Do you think someone might be changing your dad's lab results because they want to harm him, or because they have something against him personally? Or do you think it's just something happening with the system itself, without any connection to your dad specifically?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the motive behind the delusion (whether someone wants to harm the dad or has a personal vendetta versus a systemic issue), which attempts to further characterize the nature of the delusion (persecutory vs. other). The symptom profile describes the delusion itself (someone changing/holding back results) but does not specify the perceived motive behind the alteration.

patient.answer:
I don't... I don't know why you keep asking me things like this. 

No one is trying to hurt him. He's just... he's just an old man. Why would anyone care about him personally? It's just... the numbers. The numbers in the system don't match what they should be. That's all. I don't know who is doing it or why. I just know it's happening.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has any delusional ideas beyond the specific belief about lab result manipulation, which would help differentiate F22.0 (paranoid type) from F22.9 (unspecified type).
doctor.question: Besides the lab results, do you believe there are other ways people might be acting against you or deceiving you in your life—like at work, with your family, or anywhere else? Or is it really just about your dad's lab numbers?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw and it’s wearing me down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether my delusional beliefs extend beyond the specific situation with my dad's lab numbers. This relates to the scope of my delusion, which is covered by S019.

patient.answer:
No... it's just the labs. I don't know why you keep digging for other things. 

For the past year, I've just... I've only been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing them. Or holding parts of his results back. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine—the doctors, my family—but they aren't. I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. 

It's just... it's really wearing me down. That's all this is about. Just the numbers.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has any insight into the possibility that their belief might be incorrect (insight into illness), which would help differentiate F22.0 (paranoid type, typically with more conviction and less insight) from F22.9 (unspecified type, which may have varying levels of insight).
doctor.question: If you went back and looked at your dad's lab results again right now, is there any chance at all that you might have misread them the first time, or is that completely impossible?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw and it’s wearing me down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there is any chance the patient misread the lab results, testing the fixity of the belief and whether it can change in the face of contradictory evidence, which directly corresponds to the Delusions symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I didn't misread them. 

I know what I saw. I draw blood for a living, I look at these kinds of numbers all day. I... I know they don't match. I've spent a year trying to get someone to just listen and see that the clinic system is altering them or hiding things. But everyone just keeps telling me they're fine. It's... it's exhausting. But I didn't misread them. That's impossible.

inference.note: Patient demonstrates a circumscribed, non-bizarre delusion focused solely on lab result manipulation. Lacks ideas of reference, persecution, or grandiosity. No hallucinations. Maintains functioning in work and daily activities. No evidence of systematized delusional system or secondary elaborations. Meets criteria for Delusional Disorder, Erotomanic Type is ruled out (no romantic focus). Persecutory Type is ruled out (no belief in being harmed or conspired against). F22.9 (unspecified) no longer needed given clear presentation of isolated delusion.

opening_question.intent: Establish rapport and identify the chief complaint that brings the patient to the clinic
opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, circumscribed delusional belief (that clinic staff are altering his father's lab results) held with absolute conviction despite contradictory evidence from multiple credible sources (family, doctors). The delusion is non-bizarre, internally consistent within its narrow scope, and has persisted for one year. Notably absent are hallucinations, formal thought disorder, prominent negative symptoms, or mood disturbance. The patient maintains functional capacity in work and daily activities, with no evidence of acute psychotic features or mood episode. This presentation is consistent with delusional disorder, somatic type (F22.0), rather than brief psychotic disorder or other psychotic conditions.
